title: Attendance Day Context
summary: Date-by-date attendance, leave, punches and gaps for an employee.
description:
Report, date by date, what attendance already exists for an employee and what is missing — before creating any Attendance Request or regularization.

Pass `employee` (an ID like ST-EMP-00026, never a person's name), `from_date`, and optionally `to_date` (defaults to from_date).

For each date returns: the weekday, whether it is a holiday or week off, any Attendance record already marked (with its status and docstatus), any Leave Application covering it, any Attendance Request already raised for it, the Employee Checkin punches with their times, whether the day is a mispunch (exactly one punch), whether it is an unexplained gap, and any task deadlines falling that day.

`summary` names the dates that matter: `unaccounted_dates` (no attendance, no leave, no request, not a holiday), `mispunch_dates`, `already_marked`, `on_leave`, `holidays`, and `dates_beyond_backdated_window` — dates too far in the past for HR Settings to allow a backdated Attendance Request.

Also returns the shift covering the window and its timings. Read-only: nothing is created or changed.

title: Interview Feedback Context
description:
Everything around one interview except the transcript: the rubric, the candidate, the panel, and the feedback records already waiting.

Call this first. It returns:
  - `rubric.skills`: the exact and complete list of skills this round is scored on, each with its own `rating_scale` (they differ per skill) and what to look for. This is the whole list -- the Interview Feedback form does not allow rows to be added, so a skill that is not here cannot be rated at all.
  - `applicant`: who is being interviewed, their designation and the opening
  - `panel`: the interviewers, with the user each feedback record belongs to
  - `feedback_records`: the Interview Feedback already on this interview -- one draft per interviewer is created automatically when the panel is set, so drafts existing is normal. Each says whether it is Draft or Submitted, and which skills the interviewer has already rated themselves.
  - `write_mode`, `require_evidence`, `unrated_skill_policy`: the rules your write will be held to.
  - `guards`: blocking problems. If this list is not empty, do what it says and stop.

Read-only.

title: Interview Transcript
description:
Fetch the transcript of one interview, normalised, whoever recorded it.

Walks the transcript sources configured in Interview Feedback Agent Settings in order and returns the first one that yields dialogue, so you do not need to know -- or ask -- which tool recorded this interview. WebVTT, SRT, JSON exports and plain text all come back in the same shape.

Returns `found`, an `attempts` list saying what was tried and what each source gave back, and when something was found a `transcript` carrying:
  - `source` and `format`: where it came from and how it was read
  - `speakers`: each voice with its `role` (Interviewer, Candidate, or null when it could not be established), turn count and word count
  - `text`: the transcript as `[time] Speaker [Role]: what they said` lines
  - `total_chars`, `offset`, `next_offset`: call again with `offset = next_offset` to read the rest. A long interview arrives in several windows and the later ones matter most.
  - `usable`: false when the transcript is too short to assess anyone on
  - `warnings`: read these. They tell you when a role could not be established.

Only lines from a speaker whose role is Candidate are evidence about the candidate. If `found` is false, there is nothing to assess -- report the attempts and stop.

title: Interview Skill Score Context
summary: Compulsory skills for one PMS Job Applicant Skill Review's designation, and any ratings already recorded.
description:
Call this first, and call it again after your last record_skill_scores batch to confirm you are actually done. Pass the PMS Job Applicant Skill Review ID (e.g. PMS-JA-REV-2026-00007) -- that is the record this agent's trigger runs against, not the interview schedule. Returns:
  - `skills`: the exact, complete list of compulsory skills for this review's Appraisal Designation, each with what it means (`what_it_means`). This can be a long list -- some designations carry 30+ compulsory skills -- which is exactly why record_skill_scores takes them in batches rather than all at once.
  - `already_scored` / `missing`: which of those skills already have a rating row on this review, and which still need one. `missing` is what is actually left to do.
  - `schedule`: the Sanskar Interview Schedule linked to this review's Interview -- pass this same review ID to interview_skill_score_transcript, which resolves the schedule and its transcript itself.
  - `asked_skills`: which of these skills were actually put to the candidate as a question on that schedule -- a hint only, from the LiveKit call agent's own record, not something you rate. A skill never asked directly can still be rated if the candidate covered it while answering something else.
  - `rating_scale`: the four points and what each means.
  - `how_to_write`: reminds you to call record_skill_scores in batches of 8-12 skills, repeatedly, rather than writing only a text summary.
  - `guards`: blocking problems (no designation, no compulsory skills configured, review already submitted, no linked schedule). If not empty, do what it says and stop.

Read-only.

title: Interview Skill Score Transcript
summary: The transcript behind one PMS Job Applicant Skill Review.
description:
Fetch the interview transcript for one PMS Job Applicant Skill Review. Pass the same review ID as interview_skill_score_context -- this tool finds the Sanskar Interview Schedule linked to the review's Interview and reads its transcript for you. There is only one source here -- the LiveKit agent that ran the call writes it directly onto that schedule -- so there is nothing to configure and nothing else to try.

Returns `found` (false when no schedule is linked, or it has no transcript yet -- report that and stop) and, when found, a `transcript` carrying `text` (as `role: what they said` lines), `total_chars`, `offset`, and `next_offset` when there is more to read. Call again with `offset` set to `next_offset` until it stops coming back -- the hard, specific answers are usually in the back half of an interview, and a score based on the first window is a wrong score.

title: Record Skill Scores
summary: Write one batch of compulsory-skill ratings onto one PMS Job Applicant Skill Review. Call repeatedly until nothing is missing.
description:
Record one BATCH of ratings for one PMS Job Applicant Skill Review -- 5 to 8 skills is a good batch size. This is NOT a single end-of-run call: a designation can carry 30+ compulsory skills, far more than fits comfortably in one function call, so call this tool AS MANY TIMES AS IT TAKES, each time with a different slice of the compulsory list, until the `missing` field in its response comes back empty.

Pass `review` (the same ID used with the other two tools) and `scores`: one entry per skill in THIS batch -- {"skill": (the exact skill name), "rating": (an integer 1 to 4), "not_applicable": (true or false), "comments": (a short quote backing it)}. Set `not_applicable` true and omit `rating` when nothing in the transcript -- neither a question nor an answer -- touched that skill; otherwise give a 1-4 rating and leave `not_applicable` false or omitted. `comments` is required either way: for a rating, the line that justifies it; for Not Applicable, a short note on why nothing touched it.

A skill mentioned only inside an answer to a different question is still real evidence -- rate it from there rather than leaving it out because no question named it.

NOT APPLICABLE VS. A RATING OF 1: not_applicable means the transcript never touched this skill at all -- no question, no answer. A rating means the skill WAS raised (asked, or brought up by the candidate) and what they said shows the level given. If your comments for a rated entry amount to "no discussion of X" / "not mentioned" / "not covered" / "no evidence of X" -- that is not_applicable, not a low rating, and this call refuses that entry rather than saving a mismarked one.

It refuses the WHOLE batch, saving nothing from it, if the review is already submitted, a skill in it is not on the compulsory list, a skill appears twice in the same batch, a rating is outside 1-4, a rating has no comments, a rating's own comments describe the skill as never having come up (that is not_applicable, not a rating), or a row carries both a rating and not_applicable. The error names exactly what was wrong -- fix that one thing and call again; a rejected batch does not need every other batch resent.

Writes onto this review's own Skill Ratings table, updating just the compulsory-skill rows THIS batch names -- any other row already there (a human's own extra skill, or a compulsory skill from a different batch) is left exactly as it is. Never submits anything, and never touches the linked Sanskar Interview Schedule or its status -- a human still reviews the ratings before marking the interview Completed. Ending the run without ever calling this tool means NOTHING was saved, no matter how thorough your final text answer looks.

title: Leave Impact Report
summary: Full dependency check for a leave request: blockers, task and project conflicts, team coverage, balance.
description:
Assemble the complete dependency picture for one leave request, in a single call, without changing anything.

Pass `leave_application` when reacting to a filed application (e.g. HR-LAP-2026-00040) — everything else is read off the record. For a what-if check on leave nobody has filed yet, pass `employee` (an ID like ST-EMP-00026, never a person's name) plus `from_date`, `to_date` and `leave_type` instead.

Returns, all cross-checked against this install's own rules and data:
- `verdict`: "clean", "needs_review" or "blocked", and `recommendation`, one line telling you what to do.
- `predicted_blockers`: things that would make the save or submit be REFUSED — no leave allocation, insufficient balance, over the leave type's continuous-day cap, missing required attachment, too little prior notice, notice period, a Leave Block List date, an overlapping application, dates before joining. Each carries the exact reason.
- `concerns`: real conflicts a human must weigh — milestones and high-priority tasks falling due inside the leave or just after the return, project deadlines in the window, teammates already on leave over the same dates, thin team coverage, probation.
- `notes`: background only. Never hold a request over a note.
- `work_dependencies`: the employee's open Tasks with their deadlines, split into due-in-window / due-soon-after / already-overdue, which are milestones, which are high priority, how far along each is, the Projects they own, and `suggested_project_details_rows` — ready-made rows for the Leave Application's custom_project_details table so each project manager can sign off on their own row.
- `team_coverage`: how many people would be left, day by day, for the immediate team (same reporting manager) and for the department.
- `leave_balance`: balance before, days requested, balance after, computed by this install's own calculation.
- `notify`: the employee's email, the reporting manager, the leave approver, and every affected project manager's email.

Nothing is created, updated or submitted, and no decision is made for you. Report the figures and messages exactly as returned; never reword a blocker.

title: Preview Salary Slip
description:
Compute an employee's salary for one month using HRMS's own payroll engine, WITHOUT creating any record. Pass the Employee ID (e.g. ST-EMP-00045, never a person's name) and a posting_date inside the month you want (e.g. "2026-08-31" for August 2026); the salary structure is taken from the employee's submitted Salary Structure Assignment unless you pass one.

Returns every earning and deduction with amounts, gross_pay, total_deduction, net_pay, rounded_total, total_working_days and payment_days, plus income_tax_slab, tax_scaffolding_complete, tax_scaffolding_issues and income_tax_note.

Nothing is saved: no Salary Slip is created and no data changes. Report the returned figures exactly as given. Never present a tax figure without checking tax_scaffolding_complete first.

title: Record Interview Feedback
description:
Record your assessment of one interview. Call this exactly once, at the end.

Pass `summary` (the written assessment, plain prose), `ratings` (one entry per skill you are rating: skill, rating_given, evidence), `unrated` (rubric skills the interview never covered) and `recommendation` ('Cleared', 'Rejected' or 'Inconclusive').

Where it lands is configuration, not your decision: either a comment on the Interview, or the interviewers' existing draft Interview Feedback records. Either way it is a DRAFT. This tool never submits anything and never sets the result on a record -- the interviewer confirms their own verdict.

It refuses the whole write, without saving anything, if a skill is not on the rubric, a rating is outside 0..rating_scale for that skill, a skill is rated twice, or a rating arrives without evidence quoted from the transcript. The error names exactly what was wrong; fix that one thing rather than retrying the same call.

A rubric skill the interview never touched belongs in `unrated`, not in `ratings` with a 0. Zero means the candidate failed at it; unrated means nobody asked.

If nothing at all could be rated -- the roles could not be established, the transcript is unusable, none of the rubric came up -- still call this once with `ratings` empty, every rubric skill listed in `unrated`, the reason in `summary`, and recommendation 'Inconclusive'. That is a real outcome and it belongs on the Interview where a human will see it, not only in this run's log. An empty call with nothing in `unrated` either is refused.
